# Weather Data Exploratory Analysis - Hierarchical Structure

# I. Data Import and Pre-processing

## I.1. Initial Data Loading

**Description:** This section loads essential R packages for rainfall analysis, visualization, and time series management. The comprehensive package suite includes tools for data manipulation (tidyverse), missing data analysis (VIM, mice), time series forecasting (forecast, zoo), clustering analysis (cluster, factoextra), and advanced visualization (plotly, viridis)

```{r}
# Essential packages for rainfall analysis and visualization
if (!require("pacman")) install.packages("pacman")

pacman::p_load(
  tidyverse,      # Data manipulation and visualization
  lubridate,      # Date-time handling
  corrplot,       # Correlation visualization
  VIM,            # Missing data visualization
  mice,           # Multiple imputation
  forecast,       # Time series analysis
  zoo,            # Time series objects and functions
  hydroTSM,       # Hydrological time series management
  cluster,        # Clustering analysis
  factoextra,     # Enhanced clustering visualization
  ggplot2,        # Advanced plotting
  plotly,         # Interactive plots
  reshape2,       # Data reshaping
  corrr,          # Correlation analysis
  Hmisc,          # Statistical functions
  psych,          # Psychological/statistical functions
  car,            # Regression diagnostics
  changepoint,    # Change point detection
  ecp,            # E-Divisive change point detection
  strucchange,    # Structural change detection
  knitr,          # Table formatting
  kableExtra,     # Enhanced table formatting
  DT,             # Interactive data tables
  gridExtra,      # Multiple plots arrangement
  viridis,        # Color palettes
  RColorBrewer,   # Additional color palettes
  data.table,     # Fast data manipulation
  parallel,       # Parallel processing
  doParallel,
  ggrepel# Parallel backend
)


```

## I.2. Data Cleaning and Transformation

**Description:** Implementation of a custom function to load and clean rainfall data from CSV files. The function handles multiple data quality issues including: (1) date format conversion using lubridate, (2) proper handling of trace rainfall values (converting "traces" to 0.1mm), (3) decimal separator standardization, etc.

```{r}
library(lubridate)

# Function to load and clean rainfall data
load_and_clean_rainfall <- function(file_path, sep = ";", dec = ",") {
  # Read raw data with proper encoding and decimal support
  rainfall_data <- read.csv(file_path, sep = sep, dec = dec, header = TRUE, 
                            stringsAsFactors = FALSE, fileEncoding = "latin1",
                            na.strings = c("", " ", "NA"))  # Handles empty 'void' values
  
  # Convert Dates
  if ("Dates" %in% colnames(rainfall_data)) {
    rainfall_data$Date <- suppressWarnings(dmy(rainfall_data$Dates))
  } else {
    stop("Column 'Dates' not found in dataset.")
  }
  
  # Time features
  rainfall_data$Year <- year(rainfall_data$Date)
  rainfall_data$Month <- month(rainfall_data$Date)
  rainfall_data$DOY <- yday(rainfall_data$Date)
  rainfall_data$Week <- isoweek(rainfall_data$Date)
  rainfall_data$Quarter <- quarter(rainfall_data$Date)
  
  # Station names
  rainfall_cols <- c("X5", "Km.15", "Km.8", "Pakh", "X3", "Usine", "T11", 
                     "P.Afrique", "C2", "X6", "St.Ndombo", "X1ere_Galerie", 
                     "Cite", "X2eme_Galerie", "MB3.Y", "MB.Lavage", "Taouey_2", 
                     "Bardial_1", "Bardial_2", "Bardial_W13", "Bardial_W22", "B.Bac")
  
  # Keep only existing columns
  rainfall_cols <- rainfall_cols[rainfall_cols %in% names(rainfall_data)]
  
  # Clean rainfall values
  for (col in rainfall_cols) {
    rainfall_data[[col]] <- as.character(rainfall_data[[col]])
    
    # Handle trace values
    rainfall_data[[col]][tolower(rainfall_data[[col]]) == "traces"] <- "0.1"
    
    # Convert decimal comma to dot
    rainfall_data[[col]] <- gsub(",", ".", rainfall_data[[col]])
    
    # Remove non-numeric characters except dot
    rainfall_data[[col]] <- gsub("[^0-9.]", "", rainfall_data[[col]])
    
    # Convert to numeric
    rainfall_data[[col]] <- as.numeric(rainfall_data[[col]])
    
    # Set negative values to 0
    rainfall_data[[col]][rainfall_data[[col]] < 0] <- 0
    
    # Remove extreme outliers
    rainfall_data[[col]][rainfall_data[[col]] > 300] <- NA
  }
  
  # Summary
  cleaning_summary <- data.frame(
    Original_Records = nrow(rainfall_data),
    Date_Conversion_Issues = sum(is.na(rainfall_data$Date)),
    Stations_Processed = length(rainfall_cols),
    Total_Cells_Cleaned = length(rainfall_cols) * nrow(rainfall_data)
  )
  
  return(list(
    data = rainfall_data,
    rainfall_cols = rainfall_cols,
    cleaning_summary = cleaning_summary
  ))
}

# Example usage
data_package <- load_and_clean_rainfall("BD_rain.csv")
rainfall_data <- data_package$data
rainfall_cols <- data_package$rainfall_cols
cleaning_summary <- data_package$cleaning_summary

cat("✅ Data Cleaning Summary:\n")
print(cleaning_summary)

```

## I.3. Missing Data Assessment and Quality Control

### I.3.1. Comprehensive Missing Data Assessment

**Description:** Detailed statistical assessment of data completeness for each rainfall station. This analysis calculates key metrics including: valid record counts, missing data percentages, operational periods (first to last record), data density, and descriptive statistics (mean, median, max, SD, CV). The results are formatted into an interactive HTML table with quality ratings (Excellent/Good/Fair/Poor) based on data completeness thresholds, providing a clear overview of station reliability.

```{r}
# Comprehensive missing data assessment
comprehensive_missing_analysis <- function(data, rainfall_cols) {
  
  # Basic missing data statistics
  missing_stats <- data.frame(
    Station = rainfall_cols,
    Total_Records = nrow(data),
    Valid_Records = sapply(rainfall_cols, function(x) sum(!is.na(data[[x]]))),
    Missing_Records = sapply(rainfall_cols, function(x) sum(is.na(data[[x]]))),
    Zero_Records = sapply(rainfall_cols, function(x) sum(data[[x]] == 0, na.rm = TRUE)),
    Trace_Records = sapply(rainfall_cols, function(x) sum(data[[x]] == 0.1, na.rm = TRUE)),
    Valid_Percentage = sapply(rainfall_cols, function(x) 
      round(100 * sum(!is.na(data[[x]])) / nrow(data), 2)),
    Missing_Percentage = sapply(rainfall_cols, function(x) 
      round(100 * sum(is.na(data[[x]])) / nrow(data), 2)),
    First_Record = sapply(rainfall_cols, function(x) {
      valid_dates <- data$Date[!is.na(data[[x]])]
      if(length(valid_dates) > 0) min(valid_dates) else NA
    }),
    Last_Record = sapply(rainfall_cols, function(x) {
      valid_dates <- data$Date[!is.na(data[[x]])]
      if(length(valid_dates) > 0) max(valid_dates) else NA
    }),
    Mean_Daily_Rainfall = sapply(rainfall_cols, function(x) 
      round(mean(data[[x]], na.rm = TRUE), 2)),
    Median_Daily_Rainfall = sapply(rainfall_cols, function(x) 
      round(median(data[[x]], na.rm = TRUE), 2)),
    Max_Daily_Rainfall = sapply(rainfall_cols, function(x) 
      round(max(data[[x]], na.rm = TRUE), 2)),
    SD_Daily_Rainfall = sapply(rainfall_cols, function(x) 
      round(sd(data[[x]], na.rm = TRUE), 2)),
    CV_Rainfall = sapply(rainfall_cols, function(x) {
      mean_val <- mean(data[[x]], na.rm = TRUE)
      sd_val <- sd(data[[x]], na.rm = TRUE)
      if(mean_val > 0) round(sd_val/mean_val, 3) else NA
    })
  )
  
  # Calculate operational periods
  missing_stats$Operational_Days <- as.numeric(missing_stats$Last_Record - missing_stats$First_Record) + 1
  missing_stats$Data_Density <- round(missing_stats$Valid_Records / missing_stats$Operational_Days, 3)
  
  return(missing_stats)
}

missing_comprehensive <- comprehensive_missing_analysis(rainfall_data, rainfall_cols)

# Save detailed summary to CSV
write.csv(missing_comprehensive, "rainfall_stations_summary.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# Create and display formatted table
formatted_summary <- missing_comprehensive %>%
  arrange(desc(Valid_Percentage)) %>%
  select(Station, Valid_Records, Valid_Percentage, Missing_Percentage, 
         Mean_Daily_Rainfall, Max_Daily_Rainfall, Data_Density) %>%
  mutate(
    Valid_Percentage = paste0(Valid_Percentage, "%"),
    Missing_Percentage = paste0(Missing_Percentage, "%"),
    Quality_Rating = case_when(
      as.numeric(gsub("%", "", Valid_Percentage)) >= 80 ~ "Excellent",
      as.numeric(gsub("%", "", Valid_Percentage)) >= 60 ~ "Good",
      as.numeric(gsub("%", "", Valid_Percentage)) >= 40 ~ "Fair",
      TRUE ~ "Poor"
    )
  )

# Display formatted table
table_html <- kable(formatted_summary, 
      caption = "Rainfall Station Data Quality Summary",
      format = "html") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed", "responsive")) %>%
  column_spec(8, color = ifelse(formatted_summary$Quality_Rating == "Excellent", "green",
                               ifelse(formatted_summary$Quality_Rating == "Good", "blue",
                                     ifelse(formatted_summary$Quality_Rating == "Fair", "orange", "red"))))

print(table_html)

# Save HTML table to working directory
html_filename <- "rainfall_stations_summary_table.html"
save_kable(table_html, file = html_filename)

print(paste("HTML table saved to:", html_filename))
print(paste("Working directory:", getwd()))
print(paste("Full path:", file.path(getwd(), html_filename)))

# Verify file was created
if (file.exists(html_filename)) {
  file_info <- file.info(html_filename)
  print(paste("File size:", file_info$size, "bytes"))
  print(paste("Created on:", file_info$mtime))
} else {
  warning("HTML file was not created successfully")
}

# Enhanced missing data visualization
create_missing_data_visualizations <- function(data, rainfall_cols) {
  
  # 1. Improved missing data pattern heatmap
  missing_pattern <- data %>%
    select(Date, all_of(rainfall_cols)) %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = -Date, names_to = "Station", values_to = "Rainfall") %>%
    mutate(
      Data_Status = case_when(
        is.na(Rainfall) ~ "Missing",
        Rainfall == 0 ~ "Zero",
        Rainfall == 0.1 ~ "Trace",
        Rainfall > 0.1 ~ "Measurable"
      ),
      Year = year(Date),
      Month = month(Date),
      YearMonth = paste0(Year, "-", sprintf("%02d", Month))
    ) %>%
    # Create monthly summary for better visibility
    group_by(Station, Year, Month, YearMonth) %>%
    summarise(
      Missing_Days = sum(is.na(Rainfall)),
      Total_Days = n(),
      Missing_Pct = Missing_Days / Total_Days,
      Status = case_when(
        Missing_Pct >= 0.5 ~ "Missing",
        Missing_Pct >= 0.1 ~ "Partial",
        TRUE ~ "Complete"
      ),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  
  # Create improved heatmap with better visibility
  p1 <- ggplot(missing_pattern, aes(x = factor(Month), y = Station)) +
    geom_tile(aes(fill = Status), color = "white", size = 0.3) +
    facet_wrap(~Year, ncol = 4, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c("Missing" = "#d73027",    # Red for missing
                "Partial" = "#fdae61",     # Orange for partial
                "Complete" = "#4575b4"),   # Blue for complete
      name = "Data\nStatus"
    ) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = month.abb) +
    labs(title = "Data Availability Heatmap by Station and Year",
         subtitle = "Monthly data completeness for each station",
         x = "Month", y = "Station") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 9),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7),
      strip.text = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
      legend.position = "right",
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      plot.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11),
      panel.spacing = unit(0.8, "lines")
    )
  
  # 2. Data completeness over time (unchanged as it was already good)
  completeness_over_time <- data %>%
    rowwise() %>%
    mutate(
      Available_Stations = sum(!is.na(c_across(all_of(rainfall_cols)))),
      Percentage_Available = 100 * Available_Stations / length(rainfall_cols)
    ) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  p2 <- ggplot(completeness_over_time, aes(x = Date, y = Percentage_Available)) +
    geom_line(color = "steelblue", size = 0.5) +
    geom_smooth(method = "loess", color = "red", se = TRUE) +
    labs(title = "Data Completeness Over Time",
         x = "Date", y = "Percentage of Stations Available (%)") +
    theme_minimal()
  
  # 3. Improved station operational periods with date labels
  operational_periods <- missing_comprehensive %>%
    select(Station, First_Record, Last_Record, Valid_Percentage) %>%
    mutate(
      Station = fct_reorder(Station, as.numeric(First_Record)),
      First_Year = year(First_Record),
      Last_Year = year(Last_Record),
      Period_Label = paste0(First_Year, " - ", Last_Year),
      Duration_Years = round(as.numeric(Last_Record - First_Record) / 365.25, 1)
    )
  
  p3 <- ggplot(operational_periods) +
    geom_segment(aes(x = First_Record, xend = Last_Record, 
                    y = Station, yend = Station, 
                    color = Valid_Percentage), size = 3) +
    geom_point(aes(x = First_Record, y = Station), color = "darkgreen", size = 2) +
    geom_point(aes(x = Last_Record, y = Station), color = "darkred", size = 2) +
    geom_text(aes(x = First_Record + (Last_Record - First_Record)/2, 
                 y = Station, label = Period_Label), 
             size = 3, hjust = 0.5, vjust = -0.5) +
    scale_color_viridis_c(name = "Data\nCompleteness\n(%)") +
    labs(title = "Station Operational Periods with Date Ranges",
         subtitle = "Green dots = start date, Red dots = end date",
         x = "Date", y = "Station") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9)
    )
  
  # 4. Additional summary plot showing duration and completeness
  p4 <- ggplot(operational_periods, aes(x = Duration_Years, y = Valid_Percentage)) +
    geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.7, color = "steelblue") +
    geom_text(aes(label = Station), size = 3, hjust = 0, vjust = 0, 
              nudge_x = 0.1, nudge_y = 1, check_overlap = TRUE) +
    labs(title = "Station Data Quality vs Operational Duration",
         x = "Operational Duration (Years)", 
         y = "Data Completeness (%)") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"))
  
  return(list(
    pattern_heatmap = p1, 
    completeness_trend = p2, 
    operational_periods = p3,
    duration_quality = p4
  ))
}

missing_viz <- create_missing_data_visualizations(rainfall_data, rainfall_cols)

# Display visualizations
print(missing_viz$pattern_heatmap)
print(missing_viz$completeness_trend)
print(missing_viz$operational_periods)
print(missing_viz$duration_quality)
```

### I.3.2. Temporal Missing Data Visualization

### I.3.3. Monthly Data Availability Heatmap

**Description:** Interactive heatmap visualization showing monthly data completeness patterns across all stations and years. Uses a three-tier color coding system: blue for complete months (≥50% data), orange for partial months (10-50% data), and red for missing months (\<10% data). The faceted display by year allows identification of systematic gaps and operational changes across the monitoring network.

```{r}
# Standalone code for the heatmap (p1)

# Required libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(lubridate)

# Create the missing data pattern heatmap
missing_pattern <- rainfall_data %>%
  select(Date, all_of(rainfall_cols)) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -Date, names_to = "Station", values_to = "Rainfall") %>%
  mutate(
    Data_Status = case_when(
      is.na(Rainfall) ~ "Missing",
      Rainfall == 0 ~ "Zero",
      Rainfall == 0.1 ~ "Trace",
      Rainfall > 0.1 ~ "Measurable"
    ),
    Year = year(Date),
    Month = month(Date),
    YearMonth = paste0(Year, "-", sprintf("%02d", Month))
  ) %>%
  # Create monthly summary for better visibility
  group_by(Station, Year, Month, YearMonth) %>%
  summarise(
    Missing_Days = sum(is.na(Rainfall)),
    Total_Days = n(),
    Missing_Pct = Missing_Days / Total_Days,
    Status = case_when(
      Missing_Pct >= 0.5 ~ "Missing",
      Missing_Pct >= 0.1 ~ "Partial",
      TRUE ~ "Complete"
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Create the heatmap
p1 <- ggplot(missing_pattern, aes(x = factor(Month), y = Station)) +
  geom_tile(aes(fill = Status), color = "white", size = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~Year, ncol = 4, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Missing" = "#d73027",    # Red for missing
              "Partial" = "#fdae61",     # Orange for partial
              "Complete" = "#4575b4"),   # Blue for complete
    name = "Data\nStatus"
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun", 
                          "Jul", "Aug", "Sep", "Oct", "Nov", "Dec")) +
  labs(title = "Data Availability Heatmap by Station and Year",
       subtitle = "Monthly data completeness for each station",
       x = "Month", y = "Station") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 9),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "right",
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11),
    panel.spacing = unit(0.8, "lines")
  )

# Display the heatmap
print(p1)



# Optional: Save the heatmap
ggsave("rainfall_heatmap.jpeg", plot = p1, width = 8, height = 11, dpi = 300)
```

### I.3.4. Monthly Data Availability Analysis - Fixed NA Handling

```{r}
# Monthly Data Availability Analysis - Fixed NA Handling
# Required libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(lubridate)
library(viridis)

# Function to create monthly data summary with proper NA handling
create_monthly_summary <- function(data, rainfall_cols) {
  
  # Create monthly summary for each station
  monthly_summary <- data %>%
    select(Date, all_of(rainfall_cols)) %>%
    mutate(
      Year = year(Date),
      Month = month(Date),
      Month_Name = month.abb[Month]
    ) %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = -c(Date, Year, Month, Month_Name), 
                 names_to = "Station", values_to = "Rainfall") %>%
    group_by(Station, Year, Month, Month_Name) %>%
    summarise(
      Total_Days_In_Dataset = n(),
      Valid_Days = sum(!is.na(Rainfall)),
      Missing_Days = sum(is.na(Rainfall)),
      Zero_Days = sum(Rainfall == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
      Trace_Days = sum(Rainfall == 0.1, na.rm = TRUE),
      Rain_Days = sum(Rainfall > 0.1, na.rm = TRUE),
      # Calculate actual days in month for proper completeness calculation
      Days_In_Month = days_in_month(as.Date(paste(Year, Month, "01", sep = "-"))),
      # Fix: Set completeness based on valid days / actual days in month
      Completeness_Pct = ifelse(Valid_Days == 0, NA, round(100 * Valid_Days / Days_In_Month, 1)),
      # Fix: Set rainfall statistics to NA when no valid data exists
      Total_Rainfall = ifelse(Valid_Days == 0, NA, round(sum(Rainfall, na.rm = TRUE), 1)),
      Mean_Daily_Rainfall = ifelse(Valid_Days == 0, NA, round(mean(Rainfall, na.rm = TRUE), 2)),
      Max_Daily_Rainfall = ifelse(Valid_Days == 0, NA, round(max(Rainfall, na.rm = TRUE), 1)),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    arrange(Station, Year, Month)
  
  return(monthly_summary)
}

# Create the monthly summary
monthly_data <- create_monthly_summary(rainfall_data, rainfall_cols)

# Display first few rows
cat("=== Monthly Data Summary (First 20 rows) ===\n")
print(head(monthly_data, 20))

# Save detailed summary to CSV
write.csv(monthly_data, "monthly_rainfall_summary.csv", row.names = FALSE)
cat("\nDetailed monthly summary saved to: monthly_rainfall_summary.csv\n")

# Create summary statistics by station - handle NA values properly
station_monthly_stats <- monthly_data %>%
  group_by(Station) %>%
  summarise(
    Total_Months = n(),
    # Count months with actual data (not NA)
    Months_With_Data = sum(!is.na(Completeness_Pct)),
    Complete_Months = sum(Completeness_Pct == 100, na.rm = TRUE),
    Partial_Months = sum(Completeness_Pct > 0 & Completeness_Pct < 100, na.rm = TRUE),
    Missing_Months = sum(is.na(Completeness_Pct) | Completeness_Pct == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    # Calculate averages only for months with data
    Avg_Monthly_Completeness = ifelse(Months_With_Data == 0, NA, 
                                    round(mean(Completeness_Pct, na.rm = TRUE), 1)),
    Min_Monthly_Completeness = ifelse(Months_With_Data == 0, NA, 
                                    min(Completeness_Pct, na.rm = TRUE)),
    Max_Monthly_Completeness = ifelse(Months_With_Data == 0, NA, 
                                    max(Completeness_Pct, na.rm = TRUE)),
    Total_Rainfall_mm = round(sum(Total_Rainfall, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    Avg_Monthly_Rainfall = ifelse(Months_With_Data == 0, NA, 
                                round(mean(Total_Rainfall, na.rm = TRUE), 1)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(Avg_Monthly_Completeness))

cat("\n=== Station Monthly Statistics Summary ===\n")
print(station_monthly_stats)

# Save station summary
write.csv(station_monthly_stats, "station_monthly_stats.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# Create visualization functions with proper NA handling
create_monthly_visualizations <- function(monthly_data) {
  
  # 1. Data Completeness Heatmap - NA values will appear as white/blank
  p1 <- ggplot(monthly_data, aes(x = Month_Name, y = Station, fill = Completeness_Pct)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white", size = 0.2) +
    facet_wrap(~Year, ncol = 4) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Data\nCompleteness\n(%)", 
                         option = "plasma", direction = 1,
                         na.value = "white") +  # NA values show as white
    scale_x_discrete(limits = month.abb) +
    labs(title = "Monthly Data Completeness by Station and Year",
         subtitle = "Percentage of valid days vs actual days in month (white = no data)",
         x = "Month", y = "Station") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 8),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6),
      strip.text = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold"),
      legend.position = "right",
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold")
    )
  
  # 2. Number of Valid Days Heatmap - Fix the fill and NA handling
  # Create a version of data with NA for Valid_Days when no data exists
  monthly_data_for_valid_days <- monthly_data %>%
    mutate(Valid_Days_Display = ifelse(Valid_Days == 0, NA, Valid_Days))
  
  p2 <- ggplot(monthly_data_for_valid_days, aes(x = Month_Name, y = Station, fill = Valid_Days_Display)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white", size = 0.2) +
    # Only show text labels where Valid_Days > 0
    geom_text(data = monthly_data_for_valid_days %>% filter(!is.na(Valid_Days_Display)),
              aes(label = Valid_Days_Display), size = 2, color = "white") +
    facet_wrap(~Year, ncol = 4) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Valid\nDays", option = "viridis",
                         na.value = "white") +
    scale_x_discrete(limits = month.abb) +
    labs(title = "Number of Valid Days per Month by Station and Year",
         subtitle = "Numbers shown in cells with data (white = no data)",
         x = "Month", y = "Station") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 8),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6),
      strip.text = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold"),
      legend.position = "right",
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold")
    )
  
  # 3. Monthly Rainfall Totals Heatmap - NA values show as white
  p3 <- ggplot(monthly_data, aes(x = Month_Name, y = Station, fill = Total_Rainfall)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white", size = 0.2) +
    facet_wrap(~Year, ncol = 4) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Monthly\nRainfall\n(mm)", 
                         option = "mako", direction = 1,
                         trans = "sqrt",
                         na.value = "white") +  # NA values show as white
    scale_x_discrete(limits = month.abb) +
    labs(title = "Monthly Rainfall Totals by Station and Year",
         subtitle = "Square root scale for better visibility (white = no data)",
         x = "Month", y = "Station") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 8),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6),
      strip.text = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold"),
      legend.position = "right",
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold")
    )
  
  # 4. Data Availability Timeline - handle NA values properly
  completeness_timeline <- monthly_data %>%
    mutate(Date_Month = as.Date(paste(Year, Month, "01", sep = "-"))) %>%
    group_by(Date_Month) %>%
    summarise(
      # Only calculate statistics for stations with actual data
      Stations_With_Data = sum(!is.na(Completeness_Pct)),
      Avg_Completeness = ifelse(Stations_With_Data == 0, NA, 
                               mean(Completeness_Pct, na.rm = TRUE)),
      Min_Completeness = ifelse(Stations_With_Data == 0, NA, 
                               min(Completeness_Pct, na.rm = TRUE)),
      Max_Completeness = ifelse(Stations_With_Data == 0, NA, 
                               max(Completeness_Pct, na.rm = TRUE)),
      Stations_Complete = sum(Completeness_Pct == 100, na.rm = TRUE),
      Total_Stations = n(),
      Pct_Stations_With_Complete_Data = ifelse(Stations_With_Data == 0, 0,
                                              100 * Stations_Complete / Stations_With_Data),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  
  p4 <- ggplot(completeness_timeline, aes(x = Date_Month)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Min_Completeness, ymax = Max_Completeness), 
                alpha = 0.3, fill = "steelblue", na.rm = TRUE) +
    geom_line(aes(y = Avg_Completeness), color = "darkblue", size = 1, na.rm = TRUE) +
    geom_line(aes(y = Pct_Stations_With_Complete_Data), 
              color = "red", size = 1, linetype = "dashed", na.rm = TRUE) +
    labs(title = "Data Completeness Over Time",
         subtitle = "Blue line: Average completeness | Red dashed: % of stations with complete data | Gray ribbon: Min-Max range",
         x = "Date", y = "Completeness (%)") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"))
  
  # 5. Station Performance Overview - handle NA values
  station_performance <- monthly_data %>%
    group_by(Station) %>%
    summarise(
      Months_Available = n(),
      Months_With_Data = sum(!is.na(Completeness_Pct)),
      Avg_Completeness = mean(Completeness_Pct, na.rm = TRUE),
      Total_Valid_Days = sum(Valid_Days, na.rm = TRUE),
      Total_Possible_Days = sum(Days_In_Month, na.rm = TRUE),
      # Calculate overall completeness based on actual days in months
      Overall_Completeness = ifelse(Total_Possible_Days == 0, 0,
                                   100 * Total_Valid_Days / Total_Possible_Days),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    # Filter out stations with no data for better visualization
    filter(Months_With_Data > 0) %>%
    mutate(Station = reorder(Station, Overall_Completeness))
  
  p5 <- ggplot(station_performance, aes(x = Station, y = Overall_Completeness)) +
    geom_col(aes(fill = Overall_Completeness), width = 0.8) +
    geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(Overall_Completeness, 1), "%")), 
              hjust = -0.1, size = 3) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Completeness\n(%)", option = "plasma") +
    coord_flip() +
    labs(title = "Overall Data Completeness by Station",
         subtitle = "Based on all available monthly data (stations with no data excluded)",
         x = "Station", y = "Data Completeness (%)") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
      legend.position = "none"
    )
  
  return(list(
    completeness_heatmap = p1,
    valid_days_heatmap = p2,
    rainfall_heatmap = p3,
    timeline = p4,
    station_performance = p5
  ))
}
```

# II. Time Series Visualization

## II.1. Gap Aware Time Series Plots

**Description:** Advanced time series visualization that intelligently handles data gaps by only connecting points within 3 months of each other. This approach prevents misleading visual interpolation across large gaps while maintaining continuity for continuous data segments. Each plot includes: (1) scatter points for individual observations, (2) gap-aware line segments, (3) LOESS trend smoothing, and (4) comprehensive data statistics in captions. The visualization suite includes both individual station plots and an overview faceted plot showing all stations simultaneously.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(gridExtra)
library(viridis)
library(scales)

# Function to create gap-aware time series plot
create_gap_aware_timeseries <- function(data, station_col, max_gap_months = 3) {
  # Prepare data for the specific station
  plot_data <- data %>%
    select(Date, all_of(station_col)) %>%
    rename(rainfall = all_of(station_col)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(rainfall) & !is.na(Date)) %>%
    arrange(Date)
  
  if (nrow(plot_data) == 0) {
    # Return empty plot if no data
    return(ggplot() + 
           ggtitle(paste("No valid data for station:", station_col)) +
           theme_minimal())
  }
  
  # Calculate time differences between consecutive points
  plot_data$time_diff <- c(NA, diff(plot_data$Date))
  plot_data$gap_group <- cumsum(c(FALSE, plot_data$time_diff[-1] > (max_gap_months * 30)))
  
  # Create the plot
  p <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = Date, y = rainfall)) +
    # Add points for all data
    geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 0.8, color = "#2E86AB") +
    
    # Add lines only for continuous segments (same gap_group)
    geom_line(aes(group = gap_group), alpha = 0.7, color = "#A23B72", size = 0.5) +
    
    # Styling
    labs(
      title = paste("Rainfall Time Series:", station_col),
      subtitle = paste("Lines connect points within", max_gap_months, "months"),
      x = "Date",
      y = "Rainfall (mm)",
      caption = paste("Total observations:", nrow(plot_data))
    ) +
    
    # Theme
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, color = "gray60"),
      plot.caption = element_text(size = 8, color = "gray50"),
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "gray90", size = 0.3),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "gray90", size = 0.3)
    ) +
    
    # Scale formatting
    scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 year", date_labels = "%Y", expand = c(0.02, 0)) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0.02, 0))
  
  return(p)
}

# Function to create all time series plots
create_all_timeseries_plots <- function(rainfall_data, rainfall_cols, max_gap_months = 3, ncols = 2) {
  # Create individual plots
  plot_list <- map(rainfall_cols, ~create_gap_aware_timeseries(rainfall_data, .x, max_gap_months))
  names(plot_list) <- rainfall_cols
  
  # Calculate number of rows needed
  nrows <- ceiling(length(plot_list) / ncols)
  
  # Create combined plot
  combined_plot <- do.call(grid.arrange, c(plot_list, ncol = ncols, nrow = nrows))
  
  return(list(
    individual_plots = plot_list,
    combined_plot = combined_plot
  ))
}

# Generate the plots with 3-month maximum gap
cat("🎯 Creating time series plots with maximum 3-month gaps between connected points...\n")
timeseries_plots <- create_all_timeseries_plots(
  rainfall_data = rainfall_data,
  rainfall_cols = rainfall_cols,
  max_gap_months = 3,
  ncols = 2
)

# Data availability summary function
create_data_availability_summary <- function(rainfall_data, rainfall_cols) {
  availability_summary <- rainfall_data %>%
    select(Date, all_of(rainfall_cols)) %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = -Date, names_to = "Station", values_to = "Rainfall") %>%
    group_by(Station) %>%
    summarise(
      Total_Records = n(),
      Valid_Records = sum(!is.na(Rainfall)),
      Missing_Records = sum(is.na(Rainfall)),
      Completeness_Percent = round((Valid_Records / Total_Records) * 100, 1),
      First_Record = min(Date[!is.na(Rainfall)], na.rm = TRUE),
      Last_Record = max(Date[!is.na(Rainfall)], na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    arrange(desc(Completeness_Percent))
  
  return(availability_summary)
}

# Create availability summary
availability_summary <- create_data_availability_summary(rainfall_data, rainfall_cols)

cat("📊 Data Availability Summary:\n")
print(availability_summary)

# Function to create overview plot with all stations
create_overview_plot <- function(rainfall_data, rainfall_cols, max_gap_months = 3) {
  # Prepare data
  overview_data <- rainfall_data %>%
    select(Date, all_of(rainfall_cols)) %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = -Date, names_to = "Station", values_to = "Rainfall") %>%
    filter(!is.na(Rainfall) & !is.na(Date)) %>%
    arrange(Station, Date) %>%
    group_by(Station) %>%
    mutate(
      time_diff = c(NA, diff(Date)),
      gap_group = cumsum(c(FALSE, time_diff[-1] > (max_gap_months * 30)))
    ) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  # Create overview plot
  p <- ggplot(overview_data, aes(x = Date, y = Rainfall, color = Station)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.4, size = 0.3) +
    geom_line(aes(group = interaction(Station, gap_group)), alpha = 0.6, size = 0.3) +
    facet_wrap(~Station, scales = "free_y", ncol = 4) +
    labs(
      title = "Rainfall Time Series Overview - All Stations",
      subtitle = paste("Lines connect points within", max_gap_months, "months"),
      x = "Date",
      y = "Rainfall (mm)",
      caption = "Each facet shows a different rainfall station"
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      legend.position = "none",
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 8),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
      strip.text = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"),
      plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, color = "gray60"),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    ) +
    scale_x_date(date_breaks = "2 years", date_labels = "%Y") +
    scale_color_viridis_d(option = "plasma")
  
  return(p)
}

# Create overview plot
overview_plot <- create_overview_plot(rainfall_data, rainfall_cols, max_gap_months = 3)

# Display the overview plot
print(overview_plot)

# Function to save plots
save_timeseries_plots <- function(plots_list, overview_plot, availability_summary, 
                                 output_dir = "rainfall_timeseries_plots") {
  # Create output directory
  if (!dir.exists(output_dir)) {
    dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE)
  }
  
  # Save individual plots
  iwalk(plots_list$individual_plots, ~{
    filename <- file.path(output_dir, paste0("timeseries_", .y, ".jpeg"))
    ggsave(filename, .x, width = 12, height = 6, dpi = 300)
  })
  
  # Save overview plot
  ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "overview_all_stations.jpeg"), 
         overview_plot, width = 16, height = 12, dpi = 300)
  
  # Save availability summary
  write.csv(availability_summary, 
            file.path(output_dir, "data_availability_summary.csv"), 
            row.names = FALSE)
  
  cat("💾 Plots and summary saved to:", output_dir, "\n")
}

# Uncomment to save plots
save_timeseries_plots(timeseries_plots, overview_plot, availability_summary)
```

## II.2. Time Series Visualization with Gap-Aware Line Connections

```{r}
# Time Series Visualization with Gap-Aware Line Connections
# This script creates time series plots for each rainfall station with intelligent
# line connections that only link points within 3-4 months of each other

library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(gridExtra)
library(viridis)
library(scales)

# Function to create gap-aware time series plot with LOESS smoothing
create_gap_aware_timeseries <- function(data, station_col, max_gap_months = 3, 
                                       add_loess = TRUE, loess_span = 0.3) {
  # Prepare data for the specific station
  plot_data <- data %>%
    select(Date, all_of(station_col)) %>%
    rename(rainfall = all_of(station_col)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(rainfall) & !is.na(Date)) %>%
    arrange(Date)
  
  if (nrow(plot_data) == 0) {
    # Return empty plot if no data
    return(ggplot() + 
           ggtitle(paste("No valid data for station:", station_col)) +
           theme_minimal())
  }
  
  # Calculate time differences between consecutive points
  plot_data$time_diff <- c(NA, diff(plot_data$Date))
  plot_data$gap_group <- cumsum(c(FALSE, plot_data$time_diff[-1] > (max_gap_months * 30)))
  
  # Create the plot
  p <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = Date, y = rainfall)) +
    # Add LOESS smooth trend line first (behind other elements)
    {if(add_loess && nrow(plot_data) > 10) 
      geom_smooth(method = "loess", span = loess_span, se = TRUE, 
                  color = "#E74C3C", fill = "#E74C3C", alpha = 0.2, 
                  linetype = "solid", size = 1.2)} +
    
    # Add gap-aware lines for continuous segments
    geom_line(aes(group = gap_group), alpha = 0.6, color = "#A23B72", size = 0.4) +
    
    # Add points on top
    geom_point(alpha = 0.7, size = 0.8, color = "#2E86AB") +
    
    # Styling
    labs(
      title = paste("Rainfall Time Series:", station_col),
      subtitle = paste("Gap-aware connections (≤", max_gap_months, "months) + LOESS trend"),
      x = "Date",
      y = "Rainfall (mm)",
      caption = paste("Observations:", nrow(plot_data), "| LOESS span:", loess_span)
    ) +
    
    # Theme
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, color = "gray60"),
      plot.caption = element_text(size = 8, color = "gray50"),
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "gray90", size = 0.3),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "gray90", size = 0.3)
    ) +
    
    # Scale formatting
    scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 year", date_labels = "%Y", expand = c(0.02, 0)) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0.02, 0))
  
  return(p)
}

# Function to create all time series plots
create_all_timeseries_plots <- function(rainfall_data, rainfall_cols, max_gap_months = 3, ncols = 2) {
  # Create individual plots
  plot_list <- map(rainfall_cols, ~create_gap_aware_timeseries(rainfall_data, .x, max_gap_months))
  names(plot_list) <- rainfall_cols
  
  # Calculate number of rows needed
  nrows <- ceiling(length(plot_list) / ncols)
  
  # Create combined plot
  combined_plot <- do.call(grid.arrange, c(plot_list, ncol = ncols, nrow = nrows))
  
  return(list(
    individual_plots = plot_list,
    combined_plot = combined_plot
  ))
}
```

## II.3. Time Series Visualization with CHIRPS Gap Filling

### II.3.1. Data Integration Methodology

**Description:** Implementation of a sophisticated data blending approach that combines original station observations (blue) with CHIRPS satellite precipitation estimates (red) for gap-filling. The method prioritizes original measurements when available and uses CHIRPS data only for missing periods. Analysis is limited to 2000-2025 to focus on the modern observation period with better data quality. The combined datasets are exported individually for each station, enabling further analysis and modeling.

```{r}
# Time Series Visualization with CHIRPS Gap Filling
# This script combines original rainfall station data with CHIRPS data to fill gaps
# Original data (blue) takes priority over CHIRPS data (red) when both exist
# Analysis limited to 2000-2025 period

library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(gridExtra)
library(viridis)
library(scales)

# Load CHIRPS data
cat("📥 Loading CHIRPS precipitation data...\n")
chirps_data <- read_csv("combined_precipitation_1985_2025.csv") %>%
  mutate(Date = as.Date(date)) %>%
  filter(year(Date) >= 2000 & year(Date) <= 2025) %>%
  select(Date, precipitation) %>%
  rename(chirps_rainfall = precipitation)

cat("✅ CHIRPS data loaded:", nrow(chirps_data), "records from 2000-2025\n")

# Filter original rainfall data to 2000-2025
rainfall_data_filtered <- rainfall_data %>%
  filter(year(Date) >= 2000 & year(Date) <= 2025)

cat("✅ Original rainfall data filtered:", nrow(rainfall_data_filtered), "records from 2000-2025\n")

# Function to combine station data with CHIRPS data
combine_station_with_chirps <- function(rainfall_data, chirps_data, station_col) {
  # Get station data
  station_data <- rainfall_data %>%
    select(Date, all_of(station_col)) %>%
    rename(original_rainfall = all_of(station_col)) %>%
    arrange(Date)
  
  # Merge with CHIRPS data
  combined_data <- station_data %>%
    full_join(chirps_data, by = "Date") %>%
    arrange(Date) %>%
    mutate(
      # Create combined rainfall prioritizing original data
      combined_rainfall = ifelse(!is.na(original_rainfall), original_rainfall, chirps_rainfall),
      
      # Create data source indicator
      data_source = case_when(
        !is.na(original_rainfall) & !is.na(chirps_rainfall) ~ "Original",
        !is.na(original_rainfall) & is.na(chirps_rainfall) ~ "Original",
        is.na(original_rainfall) & !is.na(chirps_rainfall) ~ "CHIRPS",
        TRUE ~ "Missing"
      ),
      
      # Create separate columns for plotting
      original_for_plot = ifelse(!is.na(original_rainfall), original_rainfall, NA),
      chirps_for_plot = ifelse(is.na(original_rainfall) & !is.na(chirps_rainfall), chirps_rainfall, NA)
    ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(Date))
  
  return(combined_data)
}

# Function to create enhanced gap-aware time series plot with CHIRPS data
create_enhanced_timeseries <- function(rainfall_data, chirps_data, station_col, max_gap_months = 3, 
                                      add_loess = TRUE, loess_span = 0.3) {
  # Combine station data with CHIRPS
  combined_data <- combine_station_with_chirps(rainfall_data, chirps_data, station_col)
  
  if (nrow(combined_data) == 0) {
    return(ggplot() + 
           ggtitle(paste("No valid data for station:", station_col)) +
           theme_minimal())
  }
  
  # Prepare data for gap-aware plotting - Original data
  original_plot_data <- combined_data %>%
    select(Date, original_for_plot) %>%
    filter(!is.na(original_for_plot)) %>%
    arrange(Date) %>%
    mutate(
      time_diff = c(NA, diff(Date)),
      gap_group = cumsum(c(FALSE, time_diff[-1] > (max_gap_months * 30)))
    )
  
  # Prepare data for gap-aware plotting - CHIRPS data
  chirps_plot_data <- combined_data %>%
    select(Date, chirps_for_plot) %>%
    filter(!is.na(chirps_for_plot)) %>%
    arrange(Date) %>%
    mutate(
      time_diff = c(NA, diff(Date)),
      gap_group = cumsum(c(FALSE, time_diff[-1] > (max_gap_months * 30)))
    )
  
  # Prepare combined data for LOESS (prioritizing original)
  loess_data <- combined_data %>%
    select(Date, combined_rainfall) %>%
    filter(!is.na(combined_rainfall)) %>%
    arrange(Date)
  
  # Create the plot
  p <- ggplot() +
    # Add LOESS smooth trend line first (using combined data)
    {if(add_loess && nrow(loess_data) > 10) 
      geom_smooth(data = loess_data, aes(x = Date, y = combined_rainfall),
                  method = "loess", span = loess_span, se = TRUE, 
                  color = "#7B68EE", fill = "#7B68EE", alpha = 0.2, 
                  linetype = "solid", size = 1.2)} +
    
    # Add gap-aware lines for CHIRPS data (red, behind original)
    {if(nrow(chirps_plot_data) > 0)
      geom_line(data = chirps_plot_data, aes(x = Date, y = chirps_for_plot, group = gap_group), 
                alpha = 0.6, color = "#E74C3C", size = 0.4)} +
    
    # Add gap-aware lines for original data (blue, on top)
    {if(nrow(original_plot_data) > 0)
      geom_line(data = original_plot_data, aes(x = Date, y = original_for_plot, group = gap_group), 
                alpha = 0.8, color = "#2E86AB", size = 0.6)} +
    
    # Add CHIRPS points (red)
    {if(nrow(chirps_plot_data) > 0)
      geom_point(data = chirps_plot_data, aes(x = Date, y = chirps_for_plot), 
                 alpha = 0.6, size = 0.6, color = "#E74C3C")} +
    
    # Add original points (blue, on top)
    {if(nrow(original_plot_data) > 0)
      geom_point(data = original_plot_data, aes(x = Date, y = original_for_plot), 
                 alpha = 0.8, size = 0.8, color = "#2E86AB")} +
    
    # Styling
    labs(
      title = paste("Enhanced Rainfall Time Series:", station_col),
      subtitle = paste("Original data (blue) + CHIRPS gap-filling (red) | 2000-2025"),
      x = "Date",
      y = "Rainfall (mm)",
      caption = paste("Original obs:", nrow(original_plot_data), 
                     "| CHIRPS gap-fill:", nrow(chirps_plot_data),
                     "| Total coverage:", nrow(loess_data))
    ) +
    
    # Theme
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, color = "gray60"),
      plot.caption = element_text(size = 8, color = "gray50"),
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "gray90", size = 0.3),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "gray90", size = 0.3),
      legend.position = "bottom"
    ) +
    
    # Scale formatting
    scale_x_date(date_breaks = "2 years", date_labels = "%Y", expand = c(0.02, 0)) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0.02, 0))
  
  # Add manual legend
  p <- p + 
    annotate("text", x = min(combined_data$Date, na.rm = TRUE), 
             y = Inf, label = "● Original data", 
             color = "#2E86AB", hjust = 0, vjust = 1.2, size = 3) +
    annotate("text", x = min(combined_data$Date, na.rm = TRUE), 
             y = Inf, label = "● CHIRPS gap-fill", 
             color = "#E74C3C", hjust = 0, vjust = 2.4, size = 3)
  
  return(p)
}

# Function to create all enhanced time series plots
create_all_enhanced_plots <- function(rainfall_data, chirps_data, rainfall_cols, max_gap_months = 3, ncols = 2) {
  cat("🎯 Creating enhanced time series plots...\n")
  
  # Create individual plots
  plot_list <- map(rainfall_cols, ~{
    cat(paste("   Processing station:", .x, "\n"))
    create_enhanced_timeseries(rainfall_data, chirps_data, .x, max_gap_months)
  })
  names(plot_list) <- rainfall_cols
  
  # Calculate number of rows needed
  nrows <- ceiling(length(plot_list) / ncols)
  
  # Create combined plot
  combined_plot <- do.call(grid.arrange, c(plot_list, ncol = ncols, nrow = nrows))
  
  return(list(
    individual_plots = plot_list,
    combined_plot = combined_plot
  ))
}

# Enhanced data availability summary function
create_enhanced_availability_summary <- function(rainfall_data, chirps_data, rainfall_cols) {
  availability_summary <- map_dfr(rainfall_cols, ~{
    combined_data <- combine_station_with_chirps(rainfall_data, chirps_data, .x)
    
    combined_data %>%
      summarise(
        Station = .x,
        Total_Days = n(),
        Original_Records = sum(data_source == "Original", na.rm = TRUE),
        CHIRPS_Records = sum(data_source == "CHIRPS", na.rm = TRUE),
        Missing_Records = sum(data_source == "Missing", na.rm = TRUE),
        Original_Percent = round((Original_Records / Total_Days) * 100, 1),
        CHIRPS_Percent = round((CHIRPS_Records / Total_Days) * 100, 1),
        Total_Coverage_Percent = round(((Original_Records + CHIRPS_Records) / Total_Days) * 100, 1),
        First_Original = ifelse(Original_Records > 0, 
                               as.character(min(Date[data_source == "Original"], na.rm = TRUE)), 
                               NA),
        Last_Original = ifelse(Original_Records > 0, 
                              as.character(max(Date[data_source == "Original"], na.rm = TRUE)), 
                              NA),
        .groups = "drop"
      )
  }) %>%
    arrange(desc(Total_Coverage_Percent))
  
  return(availability_summary)
}

# Function to create enhanced overview plot
create_enhanced_overview_plot <- function(rainfall_data, chirps_data, rainfall_cols, max_gap_months = 3) {
  # Prepare combined data for all stations
  overview_data <- map_dfr(rainfall_cols, ~{
    combined_data <- combine_station_with_chirps(rainfall_data, chirps_data, .x)
    combined_data %>%
      mutate(Station = .x) %>%
      select(Date, Station, original_for_plot, chirps_for_plot, data_source)
  }) %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = c(original_for_plot, chirps_for_plot), 
                names_to = "data_type", values_to = "rainfall") %>%
    filter(!is.na(rainfall)) %>%
    mutate(
      data_type = case_when(
        data_type == "original_for_plot" ~ "Original",
        data_type == "chirps_for_plot" ~ "CHIRPS"
      )
    ) %>%
    arrange(Station, data_type, Date) %>%
    group_by(Station, data_type) %>%
    mutate(
      time_diff = c(NA, diff(Date)),
      gap_group = cumsum(c(FALSE, time_diff[-1] > (max_gap_months * 30)))
    ) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  # Create overview plot
  p <- ggplot(overview_data, aes(x = Date, y = rainfall, color = data_type)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 0.3) +
    geom_line(aes(group = interaction(Station, data_type, gap_group)), alpha = 0.7, size = 0.4) +
    facet_wrap(~Station, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3) +
    labs(
      title = "Enhanced Rainfall Time Series Overview - All Stations (2000-2025)",
      subtitle = "Blue: Original station data | Red: CHIRPS gap-filling data",
      x = "Date",
      y = "Rainfall (mm)",
      color = "Data Source",
      caption = "Lines connect points within specified time gaps"
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 8),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
      strip.text = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"),
      plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, color = "gray60"),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      legend.position = "bottom"
    ) +
    scale_x_date(date_breaks = "5 years", date_labels = "%Y") +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("Original" = "#2E86AB", "CHIRPS" = "#E74C3C"))
  
  return(p)
}

    write.csv(combined_data, filename, row.names = FALSE)
  })
  
  cat("✅ Combined datasets exported to:", datasets_dir, "\n")
}
```

#### Gap-filling + output station name

```{r}
# Time Series Visualization with CHIRPS Gap Filling
# This script combines original rainfall station data with CHIRPS data to fill gaps
# Original data (blue) takes priority over CHIRPS data (red) when both exist
# Analysis limited to 2000-2025 period

library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(gridExtra)
library(viridis)
library(scales)

# Load CHIRPS data
cat("📥 Loading CHIRPS precipitation data...\n")
chirps_data <- read_csv("combined_precipitation_1985_2025.csv") %>%
  mutate(Date = as.Date(date)) %>%
  filter(year(Date) >= 2000 & year(Date) <= 2025) %>%
  select(Date, precipitation) %>%
  rename(chirps_rainfall = precipitation)

cat("✅ CHIRPS data loaded:", nrow(chirps_data), "records from 2000-2025\n")

# Filter original rainfall data to 2000-2025
rainfall_data_filtered <- rainfall_data %>%
  filter(year(Date) >= 2000 & year(Date) <= 2025)

cat("✅ Original rainfall data filtered:", nrow(rainfall_data_filtered), "records from 2000-2025\n")

# Function to combine station data with CHIRPS data
combine_station_with_chirps <- function(rainfall_data, chirps_data, station_col) {
  # Get station data
  station_data <- rainfall_data %>%
    select(Date, all_of(station_col)) %>%
    rename(original_rainfall = all_of(station_col)) %>%
    arrange(Date)
  
  # Merge with CHIRPS data
  combined_data <- station_data %>%
    full_join(chirps_data, by = "Date") %>%
    arrange(Date) %>%
    mutate(
      # Create combined rainfall prioritizing original data
      combined_rainfall = ifelse(!is.na(original_rainfall), original_rainfall, chirps_rainfall),
      
      # Create data source indicator
      data_source = case_when(
        !is.na(original_rainfall) & !is.na(chirps_rainfall) ~ "Original",
        !is.na(original_rainfall) & is.na(chirps_rainfall) ~ "Original",
        is.na(original_rainfall) & !is.na(chirps_rainfall) ~ "CHIRPS",
        TRUE ~ "Missing"
      ),
      
      # Create separate columns for plotting (no linking)
      original_for_plot = ifelse(!is.na(original_rainfall), original_rainfall, NA),
      chirps_for_plot = ifelse(is.na(original_rainfall) & !is.na(chirps_rainfall), chirps_rainfall, NA)
    ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(Date))
  
  return(combined_data)
}

# Function to create enhanced gap-aware time series plot with CHIRPS data (line gauge style)
create_enhanced_timeseries <- function(rainfall_data, chirps_data, station_col, max_gap_months = 3, 
                                      add_loess = TRUE, loess_span = 0.3) {
  # Combine station data with CHIRPS
  combined_data <- combine_station_with_chirps(rainfall_data, chirps_data, station_col)
  
  if (nrow(combined_data) == 0) {
    return(ggplot() + 
           ggtitle(paste("No valid data for station:", station_col)) +
           theme_minimal())
  }
  
  # Prepare data for plotting - Original data (line gauge style)
  original_plot_data <- combined_data %>%
    select(Date, original_for_plot) %>%
    filter(!is.na(original_for_plot)) %>%
    arrange(Date)
  
  # Prepare data for plotting - CHIRPS data (line gauge style)
  chirps_plot_data <- combined_data %>%
    select(Date, chirps_for_plot) %>%
    filter(!is.na(chirps_for_plot)) %>%
    arrange(Date)
  
  # Prepare combined data for LOESS (prioritizing original)
  loess_data <- combined_data %>%
    select(Date, combined_rainfall) %>%
    filter(!is.na(combined_rainfall)) %>%
    arrange(Date)
  
  # Create the plot
  p <- ggplot() +
    # Add LOESS smooth trend line first (using combined data)
    {if(add_loess && nrow(loess_data) > 10) 
      geom_smooth(data = loess_data, aes(x = Date, y = combined_rainfall),
                  method = "loess", span = loess_span, se = TRUE, 
                  color = "#7B68EE", fill = "#7B68EE", alpha = 0.2, 
                  linetype = "solid", size = 1.2)} +
    
    # Add CHIRPS line gauges (red vertical lines from 0 to value)
    {if(nrow(chirps_plot_data) > 0)
      geom_segment(data = chirps_plot_data, aes(x = Date, xend = Date, y = 0, yend = chirps_for_plot), 
                   alpha = 0.7, size = 0.8, color = "#E74C3C")} +
    
    # Add original line gauges (blue vertical lines from 0 to value, on top)
    {if(nrow(original_plot_data) > 0)
      geom_segment(data = original_plot_data, aes(x = Date, xend = Date, y = 0, yend = original_for_plot), 
                   alpha = 0.9, size = 1.0, color = "#2E86AB")} +
    
    # Styling
    labs(
      title = paste("Enhanced Rainfall Time Series:", station_col),
      subtitle = paste("Original data (blue bars) + CHIRPS gap-filling (red bars) | 2000-2025"),
      x = "Date",
      y = "Rainfall (mm)",
      caption = paste("Original obs:", nrow(original_plot_data), 
                     "| CHIRPS gap-fill:", nrow(chirps_plot_data),
                     "| Total coverage:", nrow(loess_data))
    ) +
    
    # Theme
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, color = "gray60"),
      plot.caption = element_text(size = 8, color = "gray50"),
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "gray90", size = 0.3),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "gray90", size = 0.3),
      legend.position = "bottom"
    ) +
    
    # Scale formatting
    scale_x_date(date_breaks = "2 years", date_labels = "%Y", expand = c(0.02, 0)) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0.02, 0))
  
  # Add manual legend
  p <- p + 
    annotate("text", x = min(combined_data$Date, na.rm = TRUE), 
             y = Inf, label = "█ Original data", 
             color = "#2E86AB", hjust = 0, vjust = 1.2, size = 3) +
    annotate("text", x = min(combined_data$Date, na.rm = TRUE), 
             y = Inf, label = "█ CHIRPS gap-fill", 
             color = "#E74C3C", hjust = 0, vjust = 2.4, size = 3)
  
  return(p)
}

         overview_plot, width = 18, height = 14, dpi = 300)

            file.path(output_dir, "enhanced_availability_summary.csv"),

}

}
```

## II.4. CHIRPS vs Original Data Comparison Analysis

```{r}
# CHIRPS vs Original Data Comparison Analysis
# This script analyzes the overlapping values between original station data and CHIRPS data
# Generates correlation plots, scatter plots, and statistical comparisons

library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(gridExtra)
library(viridis)
library(corrplot)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

# Load CHIRPS data (assuming you have it loaded already)
# chirps_data <- read_csv("combined_precipitation_1985_2025.csv") %>%
#   mutate(Date = as.Date(date)) %>%
#   filter(year(Date) >= 2000 & year(Date) <= 2025) %>%
#   select(Date, precipitation) %>%
#   rename(chirps_rainfall = precipitation)

# Function to get overlapping data for analysis
get_overlapping_data <- function(rainfall_data, chirps_data, station_col) {
  # Get station data
  station_data <- rainfall_data %>%
    select(Date, all_of(station_col)) %>%
    rename(original_rainfall = all_of(station_col)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(original_rainfall)) %>%
    arrange(Date)
  
  # Merge with CHIRPS data and keep only overlapping dates
  overlapping_data <- station_data %>%
    inner_join(chirps_data, by = "Date") %>%
    filter(!is.na(original_rainfall) & !is.na(chirps_rainfall)) %>%
    mutate(
      Station = station_col,
      difference = original_rainfall - chirps_rainfall,
      abs_difference = abs(difference),
      percent_difference = ifelse(original_rainfall > 0, 
                                 (difference / original_rainfall) * 100, 
                                 NA),
      rainfall_category = case_when(
        original_rainfall == 0 & chirps_rainfall == 0 ~ "Both Zero",
        original_rainfall == 0 & chirps_rainfall > 0 ~ "Original Zero, CHIRPS Positive",
        original_rainfall > 0 & chirps_rainfall == 0 ~ "Original Positive, CHIRPS Zero",
        original_rainfall > 0 & chirps_rainfall > 0 ~ "Both Positive"
      )
    )
  
  return(overlapping_data)
}

# Function to calculate comparison statistics
calculate_comparison_stats <- function(overlapping_data) {
  stats <- overlapping_data %>%
    summarise(
      Station = first(Station),
      n_observations = n(),
      correlation = cor(original_rainfall, chirps_rainfall, use = "complete.obs"),
      rmse = sqrt(mean((original_rainfall - chirps_rainfall)^2, na.rm = TRUE)),
      mae = mean(abs(original_rainfall - chirps_rainfall), na.rm = TRUE),
      bias = mean(chirps_rainfall - original_rainfall, na.rm = TRUE),
      original_mean = mean(original_rainfall, na.rm = TRUE),
      chirps_mean = mean(chirps_rainfall, na.rm = TRUE),
      original_sd = sd(original_rainfall, na.rm = TRUE),
      chirps_sd = sd(chirps_rainfall, na.rm = TRUE),
      percent_bias = (bias / original_mean) * 100,
      both_zero_pct = sum(rainfall_category == "Both Zero", na.rm = TRUE) / n() * 100,
      both_positive_pct = sum(rainfall_category == "Both Positive", na.rm = TRUE) / n() * 100,
      original_zero_chirps_pos_pct = sum(rainfall_category == "Original Zero, CHIRPS Positive", na.rm = TRUE) / n() * 100,
      original_pos_chirps_zero_pct = sum(rainfall_category == "Original Positive, CHIRPS Zero", na.rm = TRUE) / n() * 100,
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      correlation_quality = case_when(
        correlation >= 0.8 ~ "Excellent (≥0.8)",
        correlation >= 0.6 ~ "Good (0.6-0.8)",
        correlation >= 0.4 ~ "Moderate (0.4-0.6)",
        correlation >= 0.2 ~ "Weak (0.2-0.4)",
        TRUE ~ "Very Weak (<0.2)"
      )
    )
  
  return(stats)
}

# Function to create scatter plot for each station
create_scatter_plot <- function(overlapping_data, station_name) {
  # Calculate stats for subtitle
  stats <- calculate_comparison_stats(overlapping_data)
  
  # Create scatter plot
  p <- ggplot(overlapping_data, aes(x = original_rainfall, y = chirps_rainfall)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 1.2, color = "#2E86AB") +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, color = "#E74C3C", linetype = "dashed", size = 1) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "#7B68EE", fill = "#7B68EE", alpha = 0.2) +
    labs(
      title = paste("CHIRPS vs Original Rainfall:", station_name),
      subtitle = paste0("n=", stats$n_observations, " | r=", round(stats$correlation, 3), 
                       " | RMSE=", round(stats$rmse, 2), "mm | Bias=", round(stats$bias, 2), "mm"),
      x = "Original Rainfall (mm)",
      y = "CHIRPS Rainfall (mm)",
      caption = "Red dashed line = perfect agreement (1:1 line)\nBlue line = linear regression"
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, color = "gray60"),
      plot.caption = element_text(size = 8, color = "gray50"),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    ) +
    coord_fixed(ratio = 1, xlim = c(0, max(c(overlapping_data$original_rainfall, overlapping_data$chirps_rainfall), na.rm = TRUE)),
                ylim = c(0, max(c(overlapping_data$original_rainfall, overlapping_data$chirps_rainfall), na.rm = TRUE)))
  
  return(p)
}

# Function to create difference time series plot
create_difference_plot <- function(overlapping_data, station_name) {
  p <- ggplot(overlapping_data, aes(x = Date)) +
    geom_line(aes(y = difference), alpha = 0.7, color = "#E74C3C", size = 0.5) +
    geom_point(aes(y = difference), alpha = 0.5, size = 0.8, color = "#E74C3C") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
    geom_smooth(aes(y = difference), method = "loess", span = 0.3, se = TRUE, 
                color = "#7B68EE", fill = "#7B68EE", alpha = 0.2) +
    labs(
      title = paste("Rainfall Differences (Original - CHIRPS):", station_name),
      subtitle = "Positive values = Original > CHIRPS | Negative values = CHIRPS > Original",
      x = "Date",
      y = "Difference (mm)",
      caption = "Purple trend line shows temporal patterns in differences"
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, color = "gray60"),
      plot.caption = element_text(size = 8, color = "gray50"),
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    ) +
    scale_x_date(date_breaks = "2 years", date_labels = "%Y")
  
  return(p)
}

# Function to create rainfall category distribution plot
create_category_plot <- function(overlapping_data, station_name) {
  category_summary <- overlapping_data %>%
    count(rainfall_category) %>%
    mutate(
      percentage = n / sum(n) * 100,
      rainfall_category = factor(rainfall_category, 
                                levels = c("Both Zero", "Both Positive", 
                                          "Original Zero, CHIRPS Positive", 
                                          "Original Positive, CHIRPS Zero"))
    )
  
  p <- ggplot(category_summary, aes(x = rainfall_category, y = percentage, fill = rainfall_category)) +
    geom_col(alpha = 0.8) +
    geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(percentage, 1), "%\n(n=", n, ")")), 
              vjust = -0.3, size = 3) +
    labs(
      title = paste("Rainfall Agreement Categories:", station_name),
      subtitle = "Distribution of rainfall occurrence patterns",
      x = "Category",
      y = "Percentage of Observations",
      fill = "Category"
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, color = "gray60"),
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
      legend.position = "none",
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    ) +
    scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "plasma", alpha = 0.8) +
    ylim(0, max(category_summary$percentage) * 1.1)
  
  return(p)
}

# Function to analyze all stations
analyze_all_stations <- function(rainfall_data, chirps_data, rainfall_cols) {
  cat("🔍 Analyzing CHIRPS vs Original data overlaps for all stations...\n")
  
  # Get overlapping data for all stations
  all_overlapping_data <- map_dfr(rainfall_cols, ~{
    cat(paste("   Processing station:", .x, "\n"))
    get_overlapping_data(rainfall_data, chirps_data, .x)
  })
  
  # Calculate statistics for all stations
  all_stats <- map_dfr(rainfall_cols, ~{
    overlapping_data <- get_overlapping_data(rainfall_data, chirps_data, .x)
    if(nrow(overlapping_data) > 0) {
      calculate_comparison_stats(overlapping_data)
    } else {
      data.frame(Station = .x, n_observations = 0)
    }
  }) %>%
    arrange(desc(correlation))
  
  return(list(
    overlapping_data = all_overlapping_data,
    statistics = all_stats
  ))
}

# Function to create comprehensive comparison plots for each station
create_station_comparison_plots <- function(rainfall_data, chirps_data, station_col) {
  overlapping_data <- get_overlapping_data(rainfall_data, chirps_data, station_col)
  
  if(nrow(overlapping_data) == 0) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # Create individual plots
  scatter_plot <- create_scatter_plot(overlapping_data, station_col)
  difference_plot <- create_difference_plot(overlapping_data, station_col)
  category_plot <- create_category_plot(overlapping_data, station_col)
  
  # Combine plots
  combined_plot <- grid.arrange(
    scatter_plot, difference_plot, category_plot,
    ncol = 1,
    heights = c(1, 1, 1)
  )
  
  return(list(
    scatter = scatter_plot,
    difference = difference_plot,
    category = category_plot,
    combined = combined_plot,
    data = overlapping_data
  ))
}

# Function to create summary statistics visualization
create_stats_summary_plot <- function(all_stats) {
  # Correlation plot
  corr_plot <- ggplot(all_stats, aes(x = reorder(Station, correlation), y = correlation)) +
    geom_col(aes(fill = correlation_quality), alpha = 0.8) +
    geom_text(aes(label = round(correlation, 3)), hjust = -0.1, size = 3) +
    labs(
      title = "Station-CHIRPS Correlation Comparison",
      x = "Station",
      y = "Correlation Coefficient",
      fill = "Correlation Quality"
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
    coord_flip() +
    scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "plasma")
  
  # RMSE plot
  rmse_plot <- ggplot(all_stats, aes(x = reorder(Station, -rmse), y = rmse)) +
    geom_col(fill = "#E74C3C", alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_text(aes(label = round(rmse, 2)), vjust = -0.3, size = 3) +
    labs(
      title = "Root Mean Square Error (RMSE)",
      subtitle = "Lower values indicate better agreement",
      x = "Station",
      y = "RMSE (mm)"
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
  
  # Bias plot
  bias_plot <- ggplot(all_stats, aes(x = reorder(Station, bias), y = bias)) +
    geom_col(aes(fill = bias > 0), alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_text(aes(label = round(bias, 2)), 
              vjust = ifelse(all_stats$bias > 0, -0.3, 1.3), size = 3) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
    labs(
      title = "CHIRPS Bias (CHIRPS - Original)",
      subtitle = "Positive = CHIRPS overestimates | Negative = CHIRPS underestimates",
      x = "Station",
      y = "Bias (mm)",
      fill = "CHIRPS\nOverestimates"
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "#E74C3C", "FALSE" = "#2E86AB"))
  
  # Combine plots
  combined_stats_plot <- grid.arrange(corr_plot, rmse_plot, bias_plot, ncol = 1)
  
  return(list(
    correlation = corr_plot,
    rmse = rmse_plot,
    bias = bias_plot,
    combined = combined_stats_plot
  ))
}
```
